newsitem.title: USA: Neoprobe starts HIV cell therapy trials.
newsitem.headline: Neoprobe starts HIV cell therapy trials.

text.p: Neoprobe Corp said on Tuesday it began Phase I clinical studies of an activated cellular therapy which aimed to boost the immune system of HIV/AIDS patients.

The therapy, which Neoprobe acquired the rights for, involved activating lymph node cells and growing them in a culture before returning the cells to the patients to treat their disease, Neoprobe said.
The company said the therapy was similar to its RIGS/ACT cancer detection system.

"Neoprobe conducted the first ACT (activated cellular therapy) study for HIV to determine if lymphocytes from the lymph nodes of HIV-infected patients can be developed into HIV-fighting cells," said John Ridihalgh, Neoprobe's chairman and chief executive officer.

In the first study, enlarged lymph nodes were removed in an outpatient surgery. Cells from the lymph nodes were then activated and expanded in number. After surgery, the cells were reinfused into the patient to help his or her own immune system to fight HIV.

Neoprobe said the study would treat 10 HIV-positive patients with CD4 T cell counts from 100 to 500 who had no active opportunistic infections. CD4 cells were the primary cells targeted by the HIV virus.
